citation.title: Mortality and pulmonary mechanics in relation to respiratory system and transpulmonary driving pressures in ARDS
citation.trial_acronym: EPVent (parent trial; this is a secondary analysis)

provenance.quote: The EPvent study was approved by the institutional review board at the Beth Israel Deaconess Medical Center in Boston
our group tested the use of esophageal manometry for managing mechanical ventilation in patients with ARDS [15]
Subjects were monitored while supine with the head of the bed elevated to 30°. An esophageal balloon-catheter was placed, and measurements were obtained to estimate intrathoracic pressures.

Patients in the intervention group had PEEP levels adjusted to achieve a positive transpulmonary pressure of 0–10 cm H2O at end-expiration according to a sliding scale based on the fraction of inspired oxygen

Elastance of the respiratory system (ERS) was calculated as the change in airway pressure from end-expiratory hold to plateau divided by VT, and lung elastance (EL) was calculated as the change in transpulmonary pressure at the same times. The 28 day mortality was also recorded.
Of the original 61 subjects, 56 had sufficient data at baseline and 24 h to calculate DPRS and DPL for further analysis.
Fifty-six patients from a previous study were analyzed to compare PEEP titration to maintain positive transpulmonary end-expiratory pressure to a control protocol.

subgroup_flags.classification_notes: ARDS-only: enrolment required ALI/ARDS per AECC. Timing unclear: this secondary analysis reports measurements relative to study baseline in the parent EPVent trial, not relative to intubation/ICU admission. Obesity subgroup unclear: BMI not reported; only predicted body weight. Mortality ranking: 28-day mortality is the only mortality timepoint reported, so it is the longest.

extraction_flags.overlap_evidence: Confirmed per COHORTS.md and the paper text: this is a secondary analysis of the EPVent trial — 'Fifty-six patients from a previous study were analyzed' and 'The full results of the EPVent trial have been published elsewhere [15]' (reference 15 = Talmor D, Sarge T, Malhotra A et al (2008) Mechanical ventilation guided by esophageal pressure in acute lung injury, NEJM 359:2095–2104). Same cohort (56 of the original 61 EPVent patients), same centre (Beth Israel Deaconess Medical Center, Boston), same two-arm PEEP protocol. talmor_2008 is the primary report; this record sets is_primary_report: false.
unclear_items: design.randomised: the parent EPVent trial was randomised, but this paper does not restate randomisation; inferred from reference to the published EPVent trial.
eligibility.criteria.adults_18_plus: no explicit age criterion stated; adult ICU setting inferred.
design.n_centers: single centre inferred from the Beth Israel Deaconess/MGH Boston affiliation; the paper does not state the number of centres.
intervention.balloon_calibration: this paper gives no detail on balloon filling or calibration; the parent EPVent trial report would need to be consulted.

outcomes: survivor-vs-non-survivor comparisons (DPRS/DPL/ERS/EL by survival) are recorded in reported_subgroups rather than as outcome entries because they contrast groups defined by the outcome, not the intervention.
timepoint.hours for the 5 min measurements recorded as 0.08 (5/60 h) — a unit conversion of the paper's '5 min'.
extraction_flags.general_notes: Secondary/reanalysis paper: driving pressure was not a pre-specified endpoint in the parent trial ('the retrospective nature of this analysis weakens the interpretation as driving pressure was not a pre-specified endpoint in the initial study'). Correlations between ΔDPRS and ΔERS (r2 = 0.36, p < 0.0001) and ΔDPL and ΔEL (r2 = 0.65, p < 0.0001) reported in Results para 4 and Fig. 4. Text PEEP values at 5 min (12.9 vs 20.0) and 24 h (11.0 vs 19.3) differ from Table 2 PEEPtotal (15.0/21.9 and 13.1/20.6); both recorded as reported — the text values may be set PEEP rather than total PEEP. No schema field for the LOWESS analysis of DPRS vs DPL predictivity.
